🇲🇽💰 <u>2027 budget: no new taxes, 43 million kept covered</u>

Hacienda delivered Mexico's 2027 economic package to Congress: 10.6 trillion pesos in spending, growth pegged at up to 2.5%, and the deficit trimmed to 3.9% of GDP — fiscal consolidation with no new taxes. Social programs are locked in at 2.6% of GDP, reaching roughly 43 million people. The plan assumes a 3% inflation rate, a peso at 18.6 to the dollar, and oil at 54.7 dollars a barrel. (El Financiero)

🛰️🇲🇽 <u>Mexico and US down cartel drones over the border</u>

Mexico and the US launched Operativo Águila Alta to knock cartel surveillance drones out of the sky over the Tijuana-San Diego corridor — each country operating strictly within its own territory. Sedena deployed 165 specialized anti-drone units under Gen. Ricardo Trevilla, after US forces downed roughly 100 drones in the sector. Coordination, not subordination.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena rejects US-'witness' smear against senator</u>

After N+ reported that Morena senator Julieta Ramírez had signed a preliminary deal to act as a 'witness' for US authorities, she hit back: 'I demand that N+ produce the document I supposedly signed.' Morena's Ariadna Montiel backed her — 'the accusations are false; I believe Julieta, she's a very responsible young woman' — dismissing it as a manufactured black campaign against a figure eyeing Baja California's governorship.

📚🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's illiteracy rate hits a record-low 3.8%</u>

Mexico cut illiteracy from 4.1% to 3.8% in a single year — the lowest rate in the country's history. Under the National Literacy Strategy, more than 277,000 adults learned to read and write, while 323,000 finished primary school and 542,000 finished secondary. Education Secretary Mario Delgado called it 'one of the deepest acts of justice, equity and love there is.'

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Topolobampo plant: communities consulted before any decision</u>

Before ruling on the 2,200-tonne-a-day ammonia megaplant in Topolobampo, Sinaloa, Sheinbaum's government has spent about three months in assemblies with the Mayo-Yoreme communities of Ohuira Bay, reviewing the company's unfulfilled commitments and the lagoon's contamination. 'The decision hasn't been made,' the president said — the environment and interior ministries are still listening to the affected communities.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CDMX logs fewest homicides in 29 years</u>

Mexico City just recorded 43 homicides in August — its lowest monthly total in 29 years. Under Clara Brugada, high-impact crime is down 8% versus 2025 and 63% versus 2019; the daily average of high-impact crimes fell from 138 in 2019 to roughly 50 today, and vehicle theft dropped 62%.

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICAN CONSUMER CONFIDENCE HITS 12-MONTH HIGH</u>

Consumer confidence climbed to 46.1 points in August — up a full point and its highest in a year, breaking a long run of annual declines, INEGI and Banxico reported. All five components rose, led by households' willingness to buy durable goods, while expectations of higher prices eased, across a survey of 2,336 urban homes. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MORENA TO US CHAMBER: RESPECT MEXICO'S SELF-RULE</u>

After Larry Rubin, head of the American Society of Mexico, called it a "grave error" to bar dual nationals from elected office, Morena's Citlalli Hernández reminded him whose call it is: "decisions about who can hold public office belong exclusively to the people of Mexico." Her mirror — the US Constitution reserves its presidency for natural-born citizens; imagine a foreign voice branding that "a grave error." "My position is respect for the self-determination of peoples."

🌧️🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO ROLLS OUT NATIONAL CLIMATE-ALERT SYSTEM</u>

Ahead of El Niño's floods and storms, Sheinbaum's government is installing command centers nationwide — focused on the Pacific — plus a new phone-alert system to warn communities before disaster hits, run through the military's DN-III-E and Plan Marina. "The plans already exist," Sheinbaum said, "but we set out how and when to inform the population, the shelters, everything there has to be." The strategy also maps crop shifts as heat reshapes farming like Sonora's wheat.

🔎🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S SEARCH STRATEGY LOCATES 13,625 MISSING</u>

Mexico's federal search strategy has located 13,625 missing people since July 2025 — 6,939 through the Single Identity Platform and 2,572 via the National Search Alert — part of 31,946 found since October 2024, the Interior Ministry reported. Undersecretary Arturo Medina Padilla says the 10-point plan now guarantees every case "a responsible authority, forensic experts, and a formal search plan."
